grant_note: 22,184-acre Mexican land grant in present-day Orange County. Two square leagues granted 1841 by Gov. Alvarado to Santiago Arguello; three square leagues added 1846 by Gov. Pio Pico to John (Juan) Forster. Patented to Forster 1866. Acquired by Richard O'Neill Sr. and James Flood in 1882 and merged with the adjoining Rancho Mission Viejo under the O'Neill 'Rafter M' brand. Most of the former rancho is now O'Neill Regional Park, Coto de Caza, Rancho Santa Margarita, and Ladera Ranch/Rancho Mission Viejo lands.
land_attribution_warning: Rancho Trabuco (Orange County) shares its owner families (Forster, O'Neill, Flood) with the San Diego County Rancho Santa Margarita y Las Flores (now Camp Pendleton). These are DIFFERENT lands. Items in this inventory are attributed to specific counties; San Diego items encountered during searching were excluded.

Downloadable public-domain-equivalent but not downloaded (adjacent-grant, secondary to target).

items.depicts: A ranch/mission adobe on the Trabuco Mesa. LAND AMBIGUITY FLAG: catalogued as on Rancho Canada de Los Alisos (Jose Serrano grant), an OC grant ADJACENT to Rancho Trabuco -- not the Trabuco grant itself, though it shares the 'Trabuco' toponym. Described as a San Juan Capistrano Mission sub-station used for farming and cattle raising. Orange County. Additional W. view and S.E. view frames of the same adobe exist in the same collection.

items.depicts: Rancho Trabuco, Orange County -- the official U.S. Surveyor General survey plat underlying the 1866 Forster patent. LISTED in the CA State Archives USSG grant index but a digitized image was NOT located online in this pass (the Archives' Omeka portal exposes the Disenos but not this USSG plat). Likely available only as physical/microfilm at the California State Archives, or via the Bancroft land-case files.

physical_only_collections: First American Historical Photo Collection (First American Title / First American Corp.), 5 First American Way, Santa Ana, CA. Historian's office by appointment only, phone 714.250.3298; public program at firstam.com/historyoc. Holds 12,500+ OC historical photographs organized by city, dating to the late 1800s; credited source of the circa-1930 Trabuco Adobe ruins photograph and likely other Rancho Trabuco / O'Neill Ranch imagery.

Camp Pendleton Historical Society (camppendletonhistoricalsociety.org). Holds Forster & O'Neill family/ranch material -- but PRIMARILY documents the San Diego County Rancho Santa Margarita y Las Flores (now Camp Pendleton), a DIFFERENT land from OC Rancho Trabuco; use with land-attribution caution.
San Jacinto Museum (San Jacinto, Riverside County) -- credited by OC Historyland as source of a circa-1940 photograph of the Trabuco Adobe ruins; digital availability unconfirmed.

Los Angeles Corral of Westerners, 'The Branding Iron' (quarterly), June 1953 issue -- published an early copy/tracing of the Rancho Trabuco diseno; a publication rather than an online image repository.
Orange County Archives (OC Clerk-Recorder), Santa Ana -- ocrecorder.com/oc-archives; historic property documents and OC photographs (contributor to OC Stories Photos on Calisphere).
dead_ends: Library of Congress (loc.gov) -- no Rancho Trabuco photographs, Sanborn maps, or HABS/HAER records surfaced (rural ranch land, no Sanborn coverage).
David Rumsey Map Collection (davidrumsey.com) -- no Trabuco-specific map found; only a general 1866 U.S. General Land Office map of California.

Huntington Digital Library (hdl.huntington.org) -- no confirmed Trabuco/O'Neill/Rancho Mission Viejo cattle photograph; only an unrelated 'Map of the Ranchos Belonging to Abel Stearns' (Stearns did not own Trabuco).
BLM GLO Records (glorecords.blm.gov) -- confirmed a Forster/Trabuco 1866 patent exists but no directly downloadable Rancho Trabuco survey-plat image was resolved in this pass.

California Archives portal query 'SearchText=Trabuco' returned only 3 diseno items (Trabuco Rancho, Niguil Rancho, Mission Vieja or La Paz Rancho); the USSG patent plat (MC 4:4-579) is not in the online Omeka portal.
USGS topoView -- only regional historical topo sheets covering Trabuco Canyon, nothing ranch-operation-specific; not catalogued as ranch imagery.
